p.src: The story tells how Song Jiang arranged for “Ten Feet of Steel” to marry Wang Ying. Everyone praised Song Gongming’s benevolence and virtue, and another celebratory banquet was held that day. While they were feasting, a man came up from Zhu Gui’s tavern to report: “A party of travelers was passing along the main road before the woods. When our underlings went out to stop them, one of the party identified himself as Lei Heng, the chief constable of Yuncheng County, so Chief Zhu invited him to stay. He is now eating and drinking his customary allowance at the tavern, and has sent a runner ahead to inform you.” Chao Gai and Song Jiang were delighted to hear this and immediately descended the mountain with their strategist, Wu Yong, to welcome him. Zhu Gui had already brought him by boat to the shore at Golden Sands Beach. On seeing him, Song Jiang hurriedly bowed and said, “It has been long since I beheld your honored face, and I have constantly thought of you. What brings you past our humble abode today?” Lei Heng hastily returned the courtesy and replied, “I was sent by our county on official business to Dongchang Prefecture. On my way back, I passed the crossing, where the underlings stopped me and demanded road money. I gave them my humble name, and Brother Zhu therefore insisted that I stay.” Song Jiang said, “Heaven has granted us this good fortune!” They invited him into the main stronghold, introduced him to all the chiefs, and entertained him with wine. He stayed for five days in succession, conversing informally with Song Jiang each day. Chao Gai asked after Zhu Tong. Lei Heng replied, “Zhu Tong is now serving as the county jail warden, and the newly appointed magistrate thinks very highly of him.” Song Jiang tactfully broached the subject of Lei Heng joining the band on the mountain, but Lei Heng declined, saying that his mother was advanced in years and he could not yet follow them; after he had cared for her to the end of her days, he would come and join them. Lei Heng then bowed farewell and descended the mountain. Song Jiang and the others repeatedly urged him to stay, but could not detain him. Each of the chiefs presented him with gold, silver, or silk; Song Jiang and Chao Gai naturally gave gifts as well. Carrying a large bundle of gold and silver, Lei Heng descended the mountain. All the chiefs escorted him to the crossing and took leave of him; after they ferried him over to the main road, he returned alone to Yuncheng County. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now Chao Gai and Song Jiang returned to the Hall of Righteous Assembly in the main stronghold and asked their strategist, Scholar Wu, to settle the duties of the mountain fortress. At the four taverns to the east, south, west, and north they would sell wine and meat and receive worthy men coming from every quarter to join the band. Two chiefs were stationed at each tavern. “Ten Feet of Steel” and Wang the Short Tiger were to encamp below the rear of the mountain and oversee the horses. The brothers Tong Wei and Tong Meng were to guard the lesser stockade at Golden Sands Beach. The uncle and nephew Zou Yuan and Zou Run were to guard the lesser stockade at Duck’s Beak Beach. Huang Xin and Yan Shun were to command cavalry encamped along the main road before the mountain and guard it. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao were to guard the first pass before the mountain. Du Qian and Song Wan were to guard the second pass at Wanzi City. Liu Tang and Mu Hong were to guard the third pass at the entrance to the main stronghold. The three Ruan brothers were to guard the naval stockade south of the mountain. Meng Kang was to continue supervising the construction of warships. Li Ying, Du Xing, and Jiang Jing were placed in general charge of the stronghold’s grain, funds, gold, and silk. Tao Zongwang and Xue Yong were to supervise construction of the inner walls and watchtowers within Liangshan Marsh. Mu Chun and Li Yun were to supervise construction of buildings and palisades. Xiao Rang and Jin Dajian were placed in charge of all correspondence and official documents concerning guests. Pei Xuan had sole charge of the military administration office, rewarding merit and punishing offenses. p.src: Now Lei Heng left Liangshan Marsh with the bundle on his back and his broad-bladed staff-sword in hand, and took the road back to Yuncheng County. On reaching home, he paid his respects to his aged mother, changed his clothes, took the written reply, and went directly to the county offices to see the magistrate. He made his report, surrendered the official documents and endorsed papers for cancellation, then returned home to rest awhile. As before, he reported at the county offices every morning and evening to await assignments. One day, as he reached the eastern side of the county offices, he heard someone behind him call, “Chief Constable, when did you return?” Lei Heng turned to look and saw that it was Li Xiao’er, one of the county’s idle hangers-on. Lei Heng replied, “I only got home the day before yesterday.” Li Xiao’er said, “You were away for so long that you cannot know how a new traveling courtesan from the Eastern Capital recently arrived here. Her beauty and accomplishments are both unsurpassed, and her name is Bai Xiuying. The girl came to pay her respects to you, but you happened to be away on official business. She is now performing all kinds of tales and tunes at the entertainment ground. Every day there is some diversion—drama and dance, wind and string music, or singing—and crowds as dense as mountains and seas pay to watch. Why not go and take a look, Chief Constable? She truly is a splendid beauty!” Lei Heng heard this and, having leisure at the time, went straight to the entertainment ground with Li Xiao’er. At the entrance he saw many gold-lettered banners hanging, while life-sized placards were suspended from the flagpoles. On entering, he took the foremost seat at the Azure Dragon end. On the stage they were performing a comic farce. Amid the crowd, Li Xiao’er slipped away from Lei Heng and went outside in pursuit of a bowl of refreshments. When the farce ended, an old man appeared, wearing a snug skullcap and a tea-brown gauze gown fastened with a black cord. Holding a fan, he came forward and announced, “This old fellow is a native of the Eastern Capital, and my name is Bai Yuqiao. Now that I am old, I depend entirely upon my daughter Xiuying’s singing, dancing, piping, and playing to entertain honored audiences throughout the realm.” At the sound of the gong, Bai Xiuying promptly mounted the stage and bowed to all four sides. Taking up the gong beater, she struck a quick succession of notes like beans being scattered, then brought the clapper down with a sharp crack. After reciting four seven-character lines, she said, “Today’s signboard plainly announces the tale Xiuying will perform. It is a refined and romantic model of its kind, entitled ‘At Yuzhang City, Shuang Jian Pursues Su Qing.’” After her opening remarks she sang, and after singing she resumed the tale; the entire audience applauded without cease. p.src: When Bai Xiuying reached the climax of her song, Bai Yuqiao called out in rhythm: “Though we have no horse-trading arts to win your gold, our skill needs discerning folk of wit to judge it. If you worthy spectators applaud, it will show that the piece has passed muster. My daughter, step down and make a round; then we shall perform the comic play accompanied by drums.” Bai Xiuying picked up a tray and, pointing to it, cried: “It starts at the Gate of Wealth, rests on the Ground of Profit, passes over the Land of Good Fortune, and travels the Road of Prosperity. Now that it has come before your hand, do not let it pass empty.” Bai Yuqiao said, “Go around once, my daughter. All these worthy spectators are waiting to reward you.” Holding out the tray, Bai Xiuying first came before Lei Heng. He felt in the pouch at his side, only to discover that he did not have a single coin. Lei Heng said, “I forgot today and brought nothing with me. Tomorrow I shall reward you handsomely.” Bai Xiuying laughed. “If the first vinegar is not strong, all that follows will be weak. Since you, sir, occupy the foremost seat, you should set the standard with the first gift.” Lei Heng flushed crimson. “I merely happened not to bring any money. It is not that I begrudge it.” Bai Xiuying said, “Since you came to hear the singing, sir, how could you forget to bring money?” Lei Heng replied, “Giving you three or five taels of silver would mean nothing to me. It vexes me only that I forgot to bring it today.” Bai Xiuying said, “Today, sir, you have not even one coin, yet you speak of three or five taels of silver. You are merely showing us plums to quench our thirst and painting cakes to stay our hunger.” Bai Yuqiao called out, “Daughter, you have no eyes! Instead of distinguishing townsmen from country bumpkins, why do you keep asking him for anything? Move on and ask some understanding benefactor to lead off with a gift.” Lei Heng said, “How am I not a man who understands?” Bai Yuqiao said, “If you understood the ways of the pleasure quarter, dogs would grow horns on their heads.” The crowd all joined in the jeering. Lei Heng flew into a rage and cursed, “You insolent slave! How dare you insult me?” Bai Yuqiao said, “So what if I curse a cattle driver from some three-house hamlet like you?” Someone who recognized him shouted, “You must not! This is Constable Lei of our county.” Bai Yuqiao said, “More likely he is a donkey-headed fool.” Lei Heng could endure no more. He sprang straight from his chair down onto the stage, seized Bai Yuqiao, and battered him with fists and feet until his lips split and his teeth fell out. Seeing how savagely he was beating the man, the crowd rushed in and pulled them apart, then persuaded Lei Heng to go home. Everyone in the theatre scattered in an uproar.

p.src: As it happened, Bai Xiuying and the newly appointed magistrate had formerly been intimate in the Eastern Capital. She had come expressly to Yuncheng County that day to open a theatre. When the courtesan saw that Lei Heng had beaten and badly injured her father, she summoned a sedan chair and went straight to the magistrate’s residence. There she accused Lei Heng of assaulting her father and breaking up the performance, claiming that he meant to cheat her. The magistrate heard her and said furiously, “Have the complaint written at once.” This is what is called “the power of the pillow.” He had Bai Yuqiao write out the complaint, examined his wounds, and named the witnesses. Many men in the county offices were friendly with Lei Heng and went to intercede with the magistrate on his behalf. But the woman stayed constantly in the residence, wheedling and making scenes, so that the magistrate had no choice but to proceed. Without delay, the magistrate sent men to arrest Lei Heng and bring him before the court. He had him flogged in the hall, took his confession, put a cangue upon him, and sent him out to be displayed publicly as a warning. Eager to show what she could do, the woman again spoke to the magistrate and insisted that Lei Heng be displayed at the entrance to the theatre. The next day, when the woman performed again, the magistrate ordered Lei Heng to be displayed at the theatre entrance. The jailers were all constables of the same service as Lei Heng; how could they be willing to truss him up and humiliate him? The woman thought for a while. Since she had already openly set out to torment him, there was no sense in stopping halfway. She left the theatre, sat down in a teahouse, and summoned the jailers over to rebuke them: “You are all in league with him, so you let him stand at ease. His Honor the magistrate ordered you to truss him up, yet instead you do him a favor. In a little while I shall tell the magistrate. Then we shall see whether he can deal with you or not!” The jailers said, “Please do not be angry, madam. We shall go and truss him up ourselves.” Bai Xiuying said, “If you do that, I shall reward you myself.” The jailers had no choice but to go to Lei Heng and say, “Brother, there is nothing we can do. Let us make a show of tying you up for a while.” They trussed Lei Heng up in the street.

p.src: Amid the commotion, Lei Heng’s mother happened to arrive with his meal. Seeing her son trussed up there, she began to weep and cursed the jailers: “All of you serve in the yamen just as my son does. So money truly can make you do anything! Who can guarantee that he will never fall into trouble himself?” A jailer answered, “Listen to me, good mother. We too wished to show him mercy, but the plaintiff keeps watch here and insists that he be bound. There is nothing we can do about it. At any moment she threatens to report us to the magistrate and bring misery upon us. That is why we cannot spare his dignity.” The old woman said, “Who ever heard of a plaintiff personally standing guard while the accused is publicly punished?” The jailers lowered their voices and said, “Good mother, she is very close to the magistrate. A single word from her could have us dismissed. That puts us in a difficult position.” The old woman began untying the ropes herself while cursing, “What a thieving slut, to presume so far upon her influence! I shall untie these ropes and see what she can do about it!” Bai Xiuying heard her from the teahouse and came rushing over. “You old slave woman, what did you just say?” The old woman was already furious. Pointing at her, she cursed, “You cheap bitch ridden by a thousand men, crushed beneath ten thousand, and entered by every rogue—how dare you turn around and curse me!” At this, Bai Xiuying’s willow brows shot upright and her bright eyes opened wide. She screamed abuse: “You old biting pest, you poverty-stricken hag, you wretch! How dare you curse me?” The old woman said, “What if I do curse you? You are not the magistrate of Yuncheng County, after all.” Bai Xiuying flew into a rage, rushed forward, and struck the old woman with one palm, sending her staggering. As the old woman struggled to steady herself, Bai Xiuying pursued her and kept striking her with great slaps across the face. Lei Heng was a deeply filial man. Seeing his mother beaten, rage suddenly surged from his heart. He heaved up his cangue and brought it crashing down upon the crown of Bai Xiuying’s head. The end of the cangue struck her squarely, splitting her skull, and she fell face-first to the ground. When the crowd looked, they saw that Bai Xiuying’s brains had burst out and her eyeballs protruded. She lay utterly motionless, and they knew she was dead.

p.src: When the crowd saw that Bai Xiuying had been beaten to death, they seized Lei Heng and took him straight to the county yamen to lodge a complaint, where they gave the magistrate a full account of what had happened. After examining the corpse, they all returned under guard to the county yamen. Lei Heng confessed to everything without the least resistance. His mother was released into her own recognizance and sent home to await further orders. Lei Heng was put in a cangue and confined in jail. The prison warden happened to be Zhu Tong, the Beautiful-Bearded Gentleman. When Lei Heng was delivered into his custody, there was nothing he could do, so he merely prepared food and wine for him and ordered a young jailer to clean a private room in which to lodge him. A little later, Lei Heng's mother came to the jail with food. Weeping, she pleaded with Zhu Tong: “I am over sixty years old, and this boy is all I have in the world. For the sake of your long friendship as brothers, I beg you, good Warden, to take pity on my son and look after him.” Zhu Tong said, “Good mother, set your mind at ease and go home. From now on, you need not bring him food; I shall provide for him myself. If an opportunity arises, I may be able to save him.” Lei Heng's mother said, “If you save my son, you will be as parents who have given him life anew. If any misfortune befalls him, my own life will be over as well.” Zhu Tong said, “I shall keep it firmly in mind. You need not worry, good mother.” The old woman bowed her thanks and departed. Zhu Tong pondered for a whole day but could find no means of saving him. Zhu Tong personally asked someone to approach the magistrate, working every connection above and below on Lei Heng's behalf. Although the magistrate was fond of Zhu Tong, he hated Lei Heng for killing his mistress Bai Xiuying and would not listen to a word on his behalf. Moreover, that scoundrel Bai Yuqiao kept pressing the matter, building up the case and demanding that the magistrate sentence Lei Heng to pay with his life. After Lei Heng had spent sixty days in jail, the prescribed term expired and judgment was passed. p.src: With a dozen or so young jailers, Zhu Tong escorted Lei Heng out of Yuncheng County. After they had gone some ten-odd li, they came upon a wineshop. Zhu Tong said, “Let us all go in here and have a couple of bowls of wine.” They all entered the shop to drink. Zhu Tong took Lei Heng aside alone, pretending that he needed to relieve himself. In a secluded place behind the shop he opened the cangue and released him, instructing him: “Brother, go back at once. Fetch your old mother from home and flee somewhere else by night. I shall answer the charges here in your place.” Lei Heng said, “It is well enough for me to escape, but it will surely bring trouble upon you, brother.” Zhu Tong said, “Brother, you do not understand. The magistrate resents you for killing his mistress and has made the case against you conclusive. Once you reach the prefecture, they will certainly make you pay with your life. If I release you, my offense at least does not merit death. Besides, I have no parents to worry about, and my property is more than sufficient to pay any damages. Think of the long future before you, and go.” Lei Heng bowed his thanks, then hurried home by a back gate and a narrow path. Gathering his valuables into a bundle, he took his old mother and traveled through the night to join the band at Liangshan Marsh. Of him, no more need be said for now.

p.src: Now Zhu Tong took the empty cangue and flung it into the grass. Coming back out to the young jailers, he said, “Lei Heng has escaped! What are we to do?” They replied, “Let us hurry to his home and seize him.” Zhu Tong deliberately delayed for quite some time. Reckoning that Lei Heng had gone far enough, he led the others back to the county yamen to report the escape. Zhu Tong stated, “Through my own carelessness, Lei Heng escaped on the road. He remains at large and has not been captured. I willingly accept punishment and have nothing to say in my defense.” The magistrate had always been fond of Zhu Tong and meant to accommodate him and secure his release. But Bai Yuqiao threatened to complain to the higher authorities that Zhu Tong had deliberately set Lei Heng free, so the magistrate had no choice but to report the circumstances of Zhu Tong's offense to Jizhou. Zhu Tong's household sent men to the prefectural offices to spend money and smooth the way. When Zhu Tong was escorted to Jizhou, he was openly examined in the hall; he was sentenced to twenty strokes across the back, tattooed, and exiled to the prison colony at Cangzhou. Zhu Tong had no choice but to put on a traveling cangue. Two escort officers took charge of the case documents and conducted him onto the road. His household sent along clothing and traveling expenses and first gave generous gifts to the two officers. They left Yuncheng County and made their way toward Cangzhou in Henghai Commandery. Nothing of note occurred along the road. On reaching Cangzhou, they entered the city and proceeded to the prefectural yamen. The prefect had just taken his seat in the hall, so the two officers brought Zhu Tong below the steps and presented their official papers. The prefect read the papers and saw that Zhu Tong was a man of extraordinary appearance: his face was the color of a ripe date, and his splendid beard hung below his belly. At once the prefect was already eight parts pleased with him. He ordered that the prisoner not be sent down to the prison colony but be retained at his own residence to await his commands. The traveling cangue was removed at once, and a receipt was issued. The two officers took their leave and returned home.

I told them of the kindness you had shown me, and Song Gongming likewise remembered with gratitude how you once released him. Heavenly King Chao and all the other chiefs are deeply grateful as well. For that reason, they specially sent Strategist Wu and me to visit you.” Zhu Tong asked, “Where is Master Wu now?” Wu the Scholar stepped out from behind them and said, “Wu Yong is here.” With that, he bowed. Zhu Tong hurriedly returned the courtesy, saying, “It has been a long time since we met, sir. I trust you have been well.” Wu the Scholar said, “All the chiefs in the stronghold send you their warmest regards. This time they have sent Wu Yong and Constable Lei expressly to invite you up the mountain to join us in our great cause. We have been here for many days but dared not show ourselves. Tonight at last we found a chance to meet you. I beg you, brother, to condescend to come with us to the stronghold at once and fulfill the wishes of Lords Chao and Song.” After hearing him out, Zhu Tong was unable to answer for quite some time. At last he said, “You are mistaken, sir! Say no more of this. It would be ill if outsiders overheard us. Brother Lei Heng had committed a capital crime. For friendship's sake I released him, leaving him unable to remain openly in society, so he went up the mountain and joined your band. Because of him I too was sentenced and sent here. If Heaven takes pity on me, after a year or half a year of hardship I may return home and become a law-abiding citizen once more. How, then, could I willingly do such a thing? You two had best return at once. Do not remain here and bring ugly talk upon us.” Lei Heng said, “All you do here, brother, is live beneath another man's authority and wait upon him. That is no occupation for a true man of spirit. I am not trying to cajole you into going up the mountain. The truth is that Lords Chao and Song have long yearned for you to join them. Do not delay and ruin your own future.” Zhu Tong said, “Brother, what sort of talk is this? Have you forgotten that I released you because your mother was old and your household poor? And now you come here to ensnare me into betraying righteousness!” Wu the Scholar said, “Since the constable refuses to go, we shall take our leave and depart.” Zhu Tong said, “Mention my humble name and convey my respects to all the chiefs.” Together they returned to the bridge.

p.src: The man who came out was none other than Chai Jin, the ‘Little Whirlwind.’ He asked, “Who is this?” Seeing the man’s imposing bearing and refined appearance, Zhu Tong hastily saluted and answered, “I am Zhu Tong, formerly the prison warden of Yuncheng County, now banished here after being convicted of a crime. Last night I went out with the prefect’s young son to watch the river lanterns, but the ‘Black Whirlwind’ killed the boy and has now fled into your honored manor. I beg you to lend your strength, seize him, and deliver him to the authorities.” Chai Jin said, “Since you are the ‘Beauteous Beard,’ please take a seat.” Zhu Tong said, “I would not presume. May I ask your honored name?” Chai Jin replied, “My humble surname is Chai and my given name is Jin. I am the one called the ‘Little Whirlwind.’” Zhu Tong said, “I have long heard your illustrious name.” He hurriedly bowed low and added, “I never expected to have the honor of meeting you today!” Chai Jin said, “I too have long heard of the ‘Beauteous Beard.’ Please come to the rear hall, and we shall talk.” Zhu Tong followed Chai Jin straight inside. Zhu Tong said, “How did that rogue the ‘Black Whirlwind’ dare run straight into your honored manor to hide?” Chai Jin said, “Allow me to explain. All my life I have delighted in befriending gallant men of the rivers and lakes. Because my ancestors rendered the service of yielding the throne at Chenqiao, a former emperor bestowed upon our house an iron covenant inscribed in vermilion. Thus, when men who have committed offenses take refuge in my home, no one dares search it. Recently a dear friend of mine, who is also an old acquaintance of yours and now serves as a chief at Liangshan Marsh—the man called Song Gongming, the ‘Timely Rain’—sent a secret letter instructing Scholar Wu, Lei Heng, and the ‘Black Whirlwind’ to lodge at my manor and respectfully invite you to ascend the mountain and join their righteous fellowship. When you refused and would not consent, they deliberately ordered Li Kui to kill the young master, first cutting off your road home so that you would have no choice but to ascend the mountain and take a chief’s seat. Master Wu and Brother Lei, why do you not come out and join our conversation?” Wu Yong and Lei Heng emerged from a side chamber, bowed to Zhu Tong, and said, “Brother, we beg you to forgive us. All this was done on Brother Song Gongming’s command and according to his instructions. Once we reach the stronghold, everything will be made clear.” Zhu Tong said, “Your brotherly affection may be well meant, but this was far too cruel!” Chai Jin did all he could to persuade him. Zhu Tong said, “I will go, but first let me meet the ‘Black Whirlwind’ face to face!” Chai Jin said, “Brother Li, come out quickly and speak with us.” Li Kui also emerged from the side and made a deep bow. The moment Zhu Tong saw him, a nameless fire of rage flared three thousand fathoms high in his heart. Unable to contain it, he sprang up and rushed forward, determined to fight Li Kui to the death. Chai Jin, Lei Heng, and Wu Yong desperately restrained and pacified him. Zhu Tong said, “If you want me to ascend the mountain, grant me one request, and I will go.” Wu Yong said, “Never mind one request—even if there were dozens, we would grant them all.
